At last we are home. The white walls of the house bring me back to my senses. The moment the carriage rolled
sunk at the bottom of the black darkness
and the creak of the floor under its weight
I'll put out the lamp and drown in the black darkness myself
into "nothing." How good it would be to become "nothing,"
And yet there, behind my wall, something is there.
walk into the dark rooms just like that and strike a match

Who knows, perhaps my eye would manage to catch an image of people, pale, indistinct, as if off tapestries, all those who left their faces in the mirrors, their voices in the cracks and corners, their shapes in the soft horsehair stuffing of the furniture, and their shadows on the walls.
